timeline.title: Foundation
timeline.detail: By tradition, Santa Cruz de Mompox was founded on May 3, 1537, after the battle against the Kimbay cacique. Historians still debate whether it was Alonso de Heredia or Juan de Santa Cruz.

timeline.title: Erection of the town
timeline.detail: Chronicles and documents record the formal founding of the town of Santa Cruz de Mompox, a key point on the Magdalena River navigation route.

timeline.title: Encomiendas of the Magdalena
timeline.detail: Pedro de Heredia distributes 22 encomiendas in Mompox. The river workforce —rowers, carriers and boat builders— becomes the first pillar of the momposino trade.

timeline.title: Province and royal arms
timeline.detail: Philip II creates the Province of Mompox and the King of Spain grants the town its coat of arms.

timeline.title: Temples of splendor
timeline.detail: Churches such as San Agustín (1606) and Santa Bárbara (1613) are built, icons of Mompox baroque and of the town's religious life.

timeline.title: Convents and colleges
timeline.detail: The founding of the San Agustín convent and the Jesuit San Carlos college establish Mompox as a cultural and religious center of the region.

timeline.title: Patriotic Society
timeline.detail: The Patriotic Society of Commerce is founded, a reflection of the town's mercantile power on the Magdalena river network.

timeline.title: Absolute independence
timeline.detail: On August 6, Mompox proclaims its absolute independence from Spain, one of the first in the Colombian Caribbean.

timeline.title: Bolívar and Valorous City
timeline.detail: Simón Bolívar and the Admirable Campaign. On October 19 the town receives the title of Valorous City.

timeline.title: National Monument
timeline.detail: The historic center is declared a National Monument, the first step toward its protection.

timeline.title: UNESCO Heritage
timeline.detail: The historic center is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

bandera.title: Flag
bandera.alt: Flag of Santa Cruz de Mompox: white Latin cross on a red field
bandera.description: Rectangular, red with a white Latin cross in the center. The red represents the blood shed by the momposino heroes and the white cross the religiosity inherited from Spain. It was made official in 1810; that is why its resemblance to the flag of Switzerland, established in 1848, is coincidental.
bandera.credit: Flag of Mompox — BrCaLeTo, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

escudo.title: Coat of arms
escudo.alt: Coat of arms of Santa Cruz de Mompox
escudo.description: Granted by the King of Spain in 1561. Rectangular with an angle at the base, it is divided into three quarters: in the upper ones, on a gold field, a Latin cross and a palm tree; in the lower one, on blue evoking the river, a champán (riverboat) floats, a symbol of navigation. It is flanked by Justice (sword and scales) and Prudence (snake and lit lamp), with a white dog at its feet, a symbol of fidelity.
escudo.credit: Coat of arms of Mompox — SajoR, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.5)

himno.title: Anthem
himno.author: Manuel Isaac Ribón Morón
himno.note: Lyrics of the anthem of Santa Cruz de Mompox (in Spanish).
himno.coro: Loor al noble pueblo que altivo osó el primero, del fausto seis de Agosto al esplendente sol. De independencia o muerte lanzar el grito fiero, la saña desafiando del déspota español.
estrofas: Sin patria, sin derecho esclavos degradados, tres siglos de ignominia y amarga humillación, vivieron nuestros padres al yugo infame atados, inermes soportando la bárbara opresión.
Mompox La Valerosa, ejemplo da sublime de intrépido heroísmo, de varonil virtud, rompiendo la pesada coyunda que la oprime, la muerte desafiando a horrible esclavitud.
Mompox de independencia el lábaro enarbola, y en torno ve a sus hijos valientes combatir, su sangre a mares vierte la cólera española, más ellos han jurado ser libres o morir.
Al juramento fieles ardiendo en sacra llama, se arrojan al combate de Bolívar en pos, y vencedor el héroe agradecido exclama: «Caracas dióme cuna; me dio glorias Mompox».
Tenaz, sangrienta y larga fue aquella lucha cruda, que mudo el universo atónito admiró, más la justicia santa que a los libres escuda, del triunfo las coronas al oprimido dio.
Colombia, la guerra hija de la victoria, ostentase ante el mundo con noble majestad, el mundo entusiasmado contempla su alta gloria y digna la proclama de paz y libertad.

simbolos.imagenesCredit: Photos of Mompox — various authors, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain and CC BY / BY-SA).

semanaSanta.title: Holy Week
semanaSanta.tagline: One of America's oldest and most solemn religious celebrations, alive in Mompox since the 16th century.

sections.title: A centuries-old tradition
sections.text: Since colonial times, Mompox brotherhoods and nazarenos have carried the pasos through cobbled streets. The whole town prepares all year for these days.

sections.title: National heritage
sections.text: It has been celebrated since the 16th century, and in 2026 Law 2598 recognised Mompox Holy Week as National Intangible Cultural Heritage of Colombia.

sections.title: The nazarenos and paso de mano
sections.text: Dressed in robes, the nazarenos advance in a slow, rhythmic sway, moving the pasos to the band's beat. Momposinos learn this distinctive movement from childhood.

sections.title: The main days
sections.text: Maundy Thursday and Good Friday have the longest processions. They leave the Church of the Conception and San Agustín and continue until dawn, among candles and silence.

consejos: Arrive several days early: accommodation fills up.
Wear light clothing and comfortable shoes.
Respect the brotherhoods' procession and ask before taking close-up photos.
Dates change every year with the liturgical calendar. In 2027 it runs from 18 to 28 March; check the programme before you travel.
semanaSanta.historiaText: Mompox's Holy Week keeps a colonial tradition alive: processions through the historic center, brotherhoods with centuries of history and a mood of reflection that contrasts with daily life on the river. It is one of the moments when the whole town comes together.
semanaSanta.programaTitle: Eleven days, a procession every day
semanaSanta.programaIntro: In Mompox, Holy Week starts earlier than in the rest of the country: it begins on Jueves de Dolores and ends on Easter Sunday. It is usually organised like this:

programa.texto: Mompox Holy Week begins at midnight.
Procession of the Donkey (Procesión del Burrito).
Our Lady of Sorrows (las Angustias) and the Holy Ecce Homo.
Serenade to the dead: at sunset, locals go to the cemetery in their best clothes with flowers, candles and music.
The main days: night processions with the Passion floats that last until the early hours.

semanaSanta.programaNota: Times and routes change every year: check the official programme from the town hall before you travel.

festivalJazz.title: Jazz Festival
festivalJazz.tagline: Each year the colonial town becomes an open-air stage for jazz, Caribbean music and Momposino tradition beneath the stars.

sections.title: When it happens
sections.text: It is usually held in September. The 2026 edition, the twelfth, ran from 3 to 5 September with free concerts from 7 p.m. at the Parque del Jazz, organised by the Bolívar government through Icultur.

sections.title: Jazz by the churches
sections.text: Stages fill the squares and riverfront. Concerts are free and outdoors, with colonial facades as their backdrop.

sections.title: A gathering of musicians
sections.text: National and international groups meet local bands, gaita players and drummers. The result sounds unlike any other festival.

sections.title: More than concerts
sections.text: Workshops, master classes and impromptu street performances make Mompox come alive during the festival.

consejos: Bring cash and arrive early at the squares.
Dates change with each edition (usually September); check Icultur’s official channels before you travel.
festivalJazz.origenText: Festijazz turns jazz into a community gathering: local musicians and guests play in squares, cloisters and along the riverfront, and the river becomes part of the stage.
festivalJazz.escenariosStub: A festival venue. The lineup for each night is announced before the event.

secciones.title: Where it is
items: About 300 km from Cartagena and around 250 km from Barranquilla.
An island town surrounded by wetlands and rivers in the Bolívar department.

secciones.title: From Cartagena
items: A common route is a bus from Cartagena terminal toward Magangué or Mompox.
The road journey can take 4 to 6 hours depending on vehicle and season.
You can also combine a bus trip with a river boat.

secciones.title: From Barranquilla or Santa Marta
items: Take a bus toward Magangué or El Banco, then continue by bus or alternative transport to Mompox.
Allow 5 to 7 hours in total depending on connections.

secciones.title: From Bogotá
items: Check for direct flights to Mompox, or fly to Cartagena, Montería or Corozal and continue by road.
The air-and-road connection usually takes 5 to 8 hours, depending on connections and availability.

secciones.title: By air and by river
items: Check with SATENA for available flights from your city on your travel dates.
You can also combine a bus with river transportation depending on the connection point and river levels.
Always ask for the exact arrival point and the final transfer into central Mompox.

secciones.title: Practical tips
items: Book accommodation early during peak season, including Holy Week and the Jazz Festival.
Bring cash: not every shop accepts cards.
Pack light clothing, sunscreen, insect repellent and comfortable shoes for cobbled streets.
Check bus schedules before traveling; they vary by season.

guiaPractica.title: Practical guide to visiting Mompox
guiaPractica.tagline: Weather, key dates, local food, money, getting around and health: what to know before you reach the banks of the Magdalena.
guiaPractica.actualizado: Information reviewed in November 2026. Dates, prices and recommendations may change: confirm them before you travel.

secciones.title: When to go and what weather to expect
items: It is hot all year round: the average high is around 34 °C (94 °F) and nights rarely drop below 23 °C (74 °F).
February is the hottest month (highs near 38 °C / 100 °F) and November the mildest (around 32 °C / 89 °F).
The driest season runs from December to March. September, October and November are the rainiest months.
Visitor numbers peak in December, January, Holy Week and the Jazz Festival; February, March (outside Holy Week) and October are quieter.
At midday the streets empty because of the heat. At sunset the river breeze arrives and locals sit out on the sidewalks to chat: the best time for a walk.

secciones.title: Key dates
items: Holy Week 2027: from Thursday 18 March (Jueves de Dolores) to Sunday 28 March. In Mompox it lasts 11 days, with processions every day.
Holy Wednesday (24 March 2027): serenade to the dead at the cemetery, at sunset.
Jazz Festival: usually held in September. The 2026 edition ran from 3 to 5 September, with free entry at the Parque del Jazz. The 2027 dates are announced by the Bolívar government (Icultur).
Accommodation sells out for both: book months in advance.

secciones.title: What to eat and drink
items: Queso de capa: a layered cow’s-milk cheese, plain or filled with guava paste. Only a few families make it and vendors sell it around town from wooden boxes; it keeps for a few days, so it makes a good souvenir.
Artisanal fruit wines, above all corozo wine; also tamarind, sour guava or bitter orange. Many shops offer tastings before you buy.
Traditional sweets: lime, tamarind and corozo sweets, coconut balls and panochas.
Smoked butifarra and chorizo sausages, casabe and casabito. Mompox butifarra was named the best in the Caribbean at Sabor Barranquilla 2024.
For the heat: corozo juice and sour guava, hibiscus or passion fruit sodas.

secciones.title: Money
items: Bring cash in Colombian pesos: many shops, mototaxis and street vendors only take cash.
There are few ATMs and they can run out of money in high season; withdraw what you need in Cartagena, Barranquilla or wherever you set out from.
Some hotels and restaurants accept cards, but check first.

secciones.title: Getting around
items: The historic centre is best explored on foot: the churches, the riverfront and the squares are a few blocks apart.
Bicycles are one of the most common ways locals get around, and you can rent one to tour the town.
Mototaxis are handy for short hops or a one-hour tour when the heat is strong. Agree on the price before you get on.
You do not need a car inside Mompox.

secciones.title: Heat, health and wellbeing
items: Light clothing, a hat, sunscreen and a water bottle are essential. Avoid walking between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.
Wear insect repellent, especially at dusk near the river and on swamp boat trips.

Yellow fever: the US CDC recommends vaccination for all travellers to Colombia aged 9 months and over, except those visiting only Barranquilla, Cali, Cartagena or Medellín. Mompox falls within the recommendation. Get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and talk to your doctor.
In an emergency call Colombia’s national line, 123, and ask your accommodation for the nearest emergency centre.

secciones.title: River and nature
items: A sunset boat ride on the Mompox branch of the river is a classic, and the best way to see the town from the water.
Ciénaga de Pijiño: a wetland downstream explored in motorised canoes, with waterbirds, iguanas and howler monkeys. The trip back coincides with sunset over the Magdalena.
Tours leave from the riverfront; ask at your accommodation or see the Tours section.

faq.q: How many days do I need in Mompox?
faq.a: At least two days with one night. Getting there from the coast takes more than five hours by road, so it is worth staying at least one night to see the town at an easy pace and enjoy sunset on the river. Itineraries has routes for one and two days.

faq.q: Can I visit as a day trip from Cartagena?
faq.a: It is possible, but we do not recommend it: it is about 270 km and more than five hours each way. You would spend most of the day on the road.

faq.q: When is the best time to go?
faq.a: December to March is the driest period. For a quieter visit, February and March (outside Holy Week) usually have fewer visitors. To see the town at its most intense, go for Holy Week or the Jazz Festival and book well ahead.
Yes. Many businesses only take cash, and ATMs are few and can run out of money in high season.

faq.q: Does the Jazz Festival cost anything?
faq.a: In 2026 the concerts were free to attend. Check each edition’s conditions on the official channels.

faq.q: What should I take home as a souvenir?
faq.a: Filigree jewellery from the local workshops, queso de capa and a bottle of corozo wine.

faq.q: Does Mompox Holy Week have official recognition?
faq.a: Yes. Law 2598 of 2026 recognised it as National Intangible Cultural Heritage of Colombia. It has been celebrated since the 16th century.
